notes: Versions: HRM 60-201 approved 07/08/2015 (in force on 2018-02-27 per version note); Faculty Handbook capture 2017-10-12, P&T section approved 2015; AOP 13.13 revised 01/31/08, rescinded 2018-10-22 (in force on the reference date); the provost's parental-leave guideline is dated August 2011 (revised 8-10-11) and its copy was captured 2018-04-13, within the 2017-18 reference year; it carries no later version date.

The 2011 guideline is a guide for department heads that restates university policies (major medical leave, leaves of absence, P&T); HRM 60-201 and the P&T document govern where they differ. Conflict: the guideline says major medical leave is not available for adoptive mothers; HRM 60-201 (2015) allows up to six weeks of earned major medical leave for adoption or foster placement (c3, conflicting_sources; the HRM policy governs).

No employer-paid parental leave: the only paid childbirth time is the employee's own major medical balance (R1b: 0 paid weeks). Nine-month faculty accrue 15 days of major medical leave a year in the first three years of service; they do not earn personal leave.

The FMLA policy grants family and medical leave to all regular benefits-eligible (50% time or greater) employees without the statute's 12-month and 1,250-hour requirement; the University continues its health-insurance contribution for up to 12 weeks.
The guideline states that a faculty member cannot be required to stop the tenure clock, reduce workload, or take parental leave.

Not components: leave for death in the immediate family, administrative leave (jury, witness, closures, disaster volunteer), investigative leave, military leave, organ donor leave, professional leave of absence (service with a public agency; not for a birth), separation leave payout, and PERS disability retirement (separation only).

Birth parent chain: major medical leave after the birth (own balance, normally 6-8 weeks, c1) with FMLA from the start (c4 concurrent_with c1, 12 weeks) -> discretionary unpaid extension for childbirth (c5) or for illness (c6), each consecutive_after FMLA; the unpaid leave is limited to one year in all (leave_limits 52). Donated leave (c9) only for catastrophic illness, concurrent with FMLA; personal leave (c8) only for twelve-month faculty, also_available with c1.

Non-birth parent chain: FMLA 12 weeks (c4, including care of the incapacitated spouse) -> discretionary unpaid extension for childbirth (c5, consecutive_after FMLA); limited to one year in all (leave_limits 52).
